prs.author: ddullah
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: BrokenResourceError (and related stream errors) are not caught in stdout_reader, causing unhandled exceptions when the stdio_client context exits while the subprocess is still writing. Both PRs add BrokenResourceError to the exception handling in stdout_reader, just at different granularities. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: BrokenResourceError (and related stream errors) are not caught in stdout_reader, causing unhandled exceptions when the stdio_client context exits while the subprocess is still writing. prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2450 guards each individual read_stream_writer.send() call with its own try/except and returns immediately on BrokenResourceError, fixing the race at the exact callsite where it occurs. The inner-guard approach in #2450 is more precise and avoids masking read-side errors.

prs.title: fix: isolate streamable HTTP POST errors
prs.author: pragnyanramtha
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Errors in the streamable HTTP client (connection failures, HTTP 4xx/5xx responses, SSE reconnection exhaustion) are not converted to JSONRPCError responses, leaving the calling coroutine waiting forever for a reply that never arrives. Each PR patches a different location in streamable_http.py where this hang can occur, but all apply the same fix shape: catch the failure and send a JSONRPCError back through ctx.read_stream_writer. (4 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Errors in the streamable HTTP client (connection failures, HTTP 4xx/5xx responses, SSE reconnection exhaustion) are not converted to JSONRPCError responses, leaving the calling coroutine waiting forever for a reply that never arrives. Each PR patches a different location in streamable_http.py where this hang can occur, but all apply the same fix shape: catch the failure and send a JSONRPCError back through ctx.read_stream_writer. (4 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2613 is the only PR in this cluster that includes test file changes (tests/shared/test_streamable_http.py), providing verifiable coverage for the fix. It also handles HTTP error status codes at the correct abstraction layer — explicit status_code >= 400 check rather than relying on raise_for_status() bubbling through a broad catch — which is the most common real-world failure mode. #2607 catches broader Python exceptions at the handle_request_async level but has no tests. #1578 introduces a _send_error_response helper abstraction that adds indirection without benefit. #2395 only covers the reconnection-exhaustion path. The reviewer merging #2613 should fold in #2395's reconnection error path and #2607's exception-catch wrapper as additions.

members.title: Fix issue where client tool call hangs forever if server crashes or connection dies when using streamable-http
members.author: gyang-xai
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2613: Errors in the streamable HTTP client (connection failures, HTTP 4xx/5xx responses, SSE reconnection exhaustion) are not converted to JSONRPCError responses, leaving the calling coroutine waiting forever for a reply that never arrives. Each PR patches a different location in streamable_http.py where this hang can occur, but all apply the same fix shape: catch the failure and send a JSONRPCError back through ctx.read_stream_writer.

The inner-guard approach in #2450 is more precise and avoids masking read-side errors.
